lessons.title: What is a conflict?

newItems.definition: To agree to what someone else wants.
newItems.example: Do not give in too fast.

newItems.definition: To think about something overnight.
newItems.example: Sleep on it and tell me tomorrow.

mainWord.definition: Saying what you think in a calm, strong way.

lessons.mainWordForms: Assertive is an adjective. Saying what you think in a calm, strong way. Be assertive, but stay polite.
lessons.use: Use this when you tell someone to say what they think in a calm, strong way.
lessons.expressionTask: Daniel meets Sara at a community centre. What does Sara want to do?
lessons.grammar: Review: I can use conflict English in a new situation
lessons.pattern: I can use conflict English in a new situation.
lessons.task: I can ___ conflict English in a new situation.
lessons.example: I can use conflict English in a new situation.
context: Daniel meets Sara at a community centre.
Be assertive, but stay polite. A kind talk can smooth things over.
dialogue: Daniel: Sara, have you had a conflict at work?
Sara: Yes. There was an outburst in our team.
Daniel: What did you do? Did you give in?
Sara: No. I was assertive, but I stayed polite.
Daniel: Good. Sleep on it and tell me tomorrow.
Sara: Yes. A kind talk can smooth things over.

I will stay assertive and polite, and I will sleep on it tonight.'
lessons.readingQ: What does Sara say she was?
lessons.readingA: Assertive, but polite, and she did not give in.
lessons.speaking: Tell a friend about a conflict in a new situation. What did you do? How did it end?
lessons.speakingSample: I want to tell you about a conflict in a new situation. On Monday, Daniel met Sara at a community centre. Sara said, 'There was an outburst in our team. I was assertive, but I stayed polite.' Sleep on it and tell me tomorrow. A kind talk can smooth things over. A kind talk can smooth things over, and I will stay assertive.
lessons.writing: Write a short email to a friend. Tell them about a conflict in a new situation. Say what you did and how it ended.
lessons.writingSample: Dear Anna, I want to tell you about a conflict in a new situation. On Monday, Daniel met Sara at a community centre. Sara said, 'There was an outburst in our team. I was assertive, but I stayed polite. I did not give in to the angry words.' A kind talk can smooth things over. I will stay assertive and polite too. I will stay assertive and polite, and I will sleep on it tonight. Please tell me about your work. Best, Sara
lessons.sound: Assertive has its strongest beat on SER. In assertive, say SER clearly in the middle. In outburst, say OUT clearly at the start.
lessons.wordSample: It means saying what you think in a calm, strong way.
